questions.text:
enum E { A, B }
console.log(E.A)

enum E { A, B }
console.log(E[0])

enum E { A = "a" }
console.log(E.A)

enum E { A = "a" }
console.log(E["a"])

const x = "4" as unknown as number
console.log(typeof x)

const x = null!
console.log(x)

const o: { n?: number } = {}
console.log(o.n)

const t: [number, number] = [1, 2]
t.push(3)
console.log(t.length)

function f(): void {}
console.log(f())

class A { get n() { return 3 } }
console.log(new A().n)

class A { n = 6 }
console.log(new A().n)

type Id = number
const id: Id = 8
console.log(typeof id)

enum E { A = 1, B }
console.log(E.B)

const n: number | null = null
console.log(n ?? 5)

const o: { n?: { m: number } } = {}
console.log(o.n?.m)

const x: number | string = 1
console.log(typeof x)
What does structural typing compare when checking an assignment?
options: The fields and their types, not the type name
The constructor the value was created with
The file that declared the type

questions.text: What must you do before treating unknown as string?
options: Narrow it with a check the checker understands
Call a runtime function named unknown

questions.text: What does the type never mean?
options: A value that may be null
No value. The checker uses it for places control never reaches

questions.text: What does a return type annotation do?
options: It converts the returned value to that type
It registers the function in a type namespace
It throws when the runtime type differs
It checks the returned expression and does not change the value

questions.text: Which operations does a union A | B allow without narrowing?
options: Only operations that are valid for both members
Every operation of A and every operation of B
Only operations of the first member

questions.text: What does an intersection A & B require of a value?
options: That it matches A or B
That it matches both A and B
That it is a tuple of A and B

questions.text: What is keyof for?
options: It reads a property at runtime
It builds the type of keys for the checker

questions.text: What does typeof mean in type position, as in type T = typeof value?
options: It calls the JS typeof operator and stores the string
It copies the object at runtime
It takes the type of that value for the checker

questions.text: What is a type parameter on a function?
options: A per-call type chosen by the checker. It does not create another JS function
A second function created for each type
A runtime box around the argument

questions.text: What does implements change on a class?
options: Nothing at runtime. It only checks that the class matches the interface
It emits the interface as an object

questions.text: When are parameter types checked?
options: While the function runs, on each argument
They are stored in a hidden array
At compile time, at the call. They are not reified
Only if the file imports reflect-metadata

questions.text: What does any do at a use site?
options: It means the same thing as never
It prints a warning at runtime
It turns off type checking for that value

questions.text: Two object types with the same fields are assignable to each other.
A type alias can be called with new.
never can be assigned to a variable of any other type.
unknown can be assigned to string without narrowing.
A class can implement an interface.
readonly rejects a write when the JS runs.
An interface can extend another interface.
keyof is a function that exists at runtime.
A generic function is still one function after emit.
A void return annotation means the function returns null.
A ? on a property tells the checker the property may be missing.
An enum is erased the same way an interface is.
Which type accepts any value but blocks operations until you narrow it?
Which type has no values?
Which keyword declares a set of named constants that remains in JS?
Which keyword gives a type a new name and creates no value?
Which keyword checks a class against an interface?
Which type operator produces the keys of a type?
Which type operator takes the type of an existing value?
Which mark after a property name says it may be omitted?
Which mark tells the checker a value is not null or undefined?
Which keyword writes a type assertion that is erased?
Which type turns off checking at a use site?
What is the first numeric enum member when it has no initializer?
